reason: A source-code line bun prints under an error; the error's headline line is classified on its own.

match: ^\s*(severity|severity_local|code|detail|hint|where|file|line|routine|position|schema_name|table_name|column_name|constraint_name|errno)\s*:
reason: A field of a printed PostgresError object; the PostgresError line itself is classified on its own.

match: ^\[[^\]]+\] (loop|scheduler) error: <n> \|
reason: The worker runtime's headline for a caught error (worker/runtime.ts '[<worker id>] loop error:' and 'scheduler error:'); the cause (PostgresError, connection error) follows on its own line and is classified there.

match: ^api error: <n> \|
reason: The api's headline for a caught error; the PostgresError line that follows is classified on its own.

match: is immutable: (DELETE|UPDATE) is not permitted on
reason: The boot's ledger guard probes each immutable table and REQUIRES this refusal; a missing refusal is what fails the boot.

match: is append-only: row deletion is not permitted|refused by trigger \w+_append_only
reason: The boot's append-only guard probes each protected table and REQUIRES this refusal from rm_append_only_guard().

match: CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function public\.rm_\w+\(\) line|STATEMENT: DELETE FROM public\.\w+ WHERE false
reason: Postgres context lines for the guard probes' own DELETE ... WHERE false statements.

match: permission denied for table (swarm_members|swarm_recommendations|swarm_memos|swarm_sessions|swarm_briefs|swarm_subjects|swarm_session_events|swarm_session_members|swarm_subject_snapshots|swarm_session_judgements|swarm_consensus_receipts|swarm_member_keys|swarm_applications|audit_log|agent_activity_log|regime_snapshots|schema_migrations|analytics_overwrite_events)\b
reason: The boot's append-only guard probes each APPEND_ONLY_TABLES table (backend/src/db/append-only-guard.ts) with DELETE ... WHERE false as the runtime role; since D55 (6) the answer every runtime role must give is 42501, which the guard REQUIRES (PRIVILEGE_REFUSED). Seen on every 0.6 twin boot (stage-2, 2026-10-07). Limited to that table list so a missing grant elsewhere (B11) still fails; an INSERT/UPDATE denial on one of these tables is caught by verify:live and soak R8.r, not by this log line.

match: \[system-scheduler\] startup check: API unreachable at .* staying up and reporting unhealthy while the connect loop retries
reason: The scheduler starts beside the api in the replace phase and retries until the api answers ('startup check passed' follows; stage-2, 2026-10-07). An api that never answers fails readiness scheduler-authenticated and the gate's healthy-container check.

match: permission denied for table (source_acquisitions|source_acquisition_events|source_fetches|source_value_versions|analytics_ledger_methodology_versions|analytics_ledger_runs|analytics_ledger_run_events|analytics_data_vintages|analytics_vintage_members|analytics_output_snapshots|analytics_report_snapshots|swarm_brief_revisions|analytics_parity_observations)$
reason: The boot's analytics ledger guard probes each LEDGER_FAMILIES table (backend/src/db/analytics-ledger-guard.ts) with UPDATE/DELETE ... WHERE false as rm_app, which holds no UPDATE or DELETE on the ledgers (0077, D55 (6)); 42501 is the conclusive answer the guard accepts (isPrivilegeRefusal). Seen ×3 per table at every boot on stage-2, 2026-10-07.

match: ^\[system-scheduler\] initial connect failed: Unable to connect\. Is the computer able to access the url\?$
reason: The scheduler's first stream connect (scripts/lib/system-scheduler/runtime.ts start()) ran before the api listened; it then takes the same reconnect loop as every later drop (spec §3.2). An api that never answers fails readiness scheduler-initial-rebuild and the gate's healthy-container check. Seen once at boot on stage-2, 2026-10-07.

match: ERROR: canceling autovacuum task$
reason: Postgres cancels its own background autovacuum when a statement needs a conflicting lock; on the twin the migrate step's DDL does that on the freshly restored tables (seen once at 02:59:00Z on analytics_overwrite_events, stage-2, 2026-10-07). No query fails and the vacuum reruns later. Bound to the twin's restore container: production's managed Postgres is not a scanned source.

match: fetch returned <n> rows — using persisted <n> rows
reason: A live source returned nothing and the code used the real persisted floor, never synthetic data; the failed fetch itself is classified separately.

match: EDGAR MNA refresh: status=updated|\[edgar\] MNA refresh .*status=updated
reason: A successful EDGAR refresh summary; it contains the counter name 'rejected='.

match: reaper requeued/killed <n> stuck job\(s\)
reason: The worker reaper recovering jobs whose lease lapsed; the failure that caused the lapse is logged and classified on its own.

match: an upstream response is buffered to a temporary file
reason: nginx spilling a large response to disk; informational.

match: ^\S+ - - \[[^\]]+\] "(GET|HEAD|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|OPTIONS) [^"]*" [23][0-9][0-9]
reason: An nginx access-log line for a successful request; it matched an error word only through its URL, referrer or user agent (e.g. ?state=failed, a bot's .invalid URL).

match: \[api\] slow request:
reason: A request that took over 5 s: work that does not belong on the request path. Reported on every gate so none hides; issue 1079 moves the known routes (source-acquisitions, swarm/register, analytics/vintages, run-packages, telemetry, parity-sweep) off it. The 10 s limit is a decision and is never raised.

match: \[api\] request ran past the <n>s limit
reason: A request cut off at the explicit 10 s limit (v0.5.4 names the route and duration). Reported on every gate; issue 1079 owns the fix.

match: live index failed.*HTTP 413
reason: The buyback eth_getLogs scan failing on a range the provider refuses (HTTP 413). v0.5.4 halves the range, so a recurrence after v0.5.4 is a regression.

match: (pro-api\.coingecko\.com|\[gecko\]).*(HTTP 429|HTTP 40[13])
reason: The paid CoinGecko tier answering 429, 401 or 403. v0.5.4 uses the Basic plan key on the paid host, so a refusal after v0.5.4 is a regression (a bad key, or a plan limit reached).

match: geckoterminal.*(throttled|retry budget exhausted|HTTP <n> — retrying|HTTP 429)
reason: GeckoTerminal rate limiting; the code retries, then degrades to last-persisted data.

match: wallet-balances: [\w<>-]+ live read failed, degrading to last-persisted sample
reason: A wallet-balances leg could not be valued and the code degrades it to the last persisted sample (backend/src/chain/wallet-balances.ts). Two causes seen: a live price read failing (production 2026-10-01: GeckoTerminal HTTP 429, retry budget exhausted, the keyless tier v0.5.4 replaces), and the Base RPC multicall timing out (stage 2026-10-08T09:03:12Z: every leg of one sample, the strategy sleeves ZYFAI-SS1 and GIZA-SS1 included). The symbol may hold a hyphen and digits. The cause is on its own lines, which the inventory does not join to this headline.

match: ^\s*wallet-balances: batched round-[\w<>]+( NAV)? multicall failed, degrading all chain legs to stale:
reason: The wallet-balances sampler's one Base RPC multicall request threw (stage 2026-10-08T09:03:12Z: the request was aborted at its timeout, a DOMException AbortError). The code marks every chain leg of that sample stale and each leg then degrades to its last persisted sample (backend/src/chain/wallet-valuation.ts aggregateAcrossBlocks); nothing is fabricated and the next scheduled sample reads again. A provider timeout, not a defect.

match: ^\s*error: [\w<>-]+ chain read unavailable$
reason: The Error a wallet-balances leg carries when its chain read degraded upstream (backend/src/chain/wallet-valuation.ts valueLeg: new Error(`${symbol} chain read unavailable`)); bun prints it under the 'live read failed, degrading to last-persisted sample' headline, which is classified on its own. Only that one code path builds this message.

match: ^\s*(stack: "abort@\[native code\]"|message: "The operation was aborted\."),$
reason: Two fields of the DOMException AbortError bun prints under the 'wallet-balances: batched round-1 multicall failed' headline when the Base RPC request hits its timeout (stage 2026-10-08T09:03:12Z). The headline is classified on its own. The inventory cannot join a field to its headline, so this rule is held to the exact two field lines and to the worker-analytics container, the only service that runs the live wallet-balances sampler (the api serves persisted samples).

match: \[extract\] fetch \S+ \((yahoo|blockchain_com|fred|defillama\w*|geckoterminal\w*|coinmetrics)\) FAILED: The operation timed out
reason: A market-data fetch timing out. Either the provider was slow, or the run's shared deadline was used up waiting on the api under analytics-ledger load (issue 1035), which shows as every fetch timing out in the same millisecond. Either way the extractor falls back to the persisted real floor, never synthetic data.

match: \[analytics-producer\] regime failed: The operation timed out
reason: The producer's regime run hit its shared fetch deadline while every provider fetch was still outstanding (production 2026-09-25 18:35:17: every source timed out in the same millisecond); no vintage is written for that slot, nothing synthetic, and the next scheduled run retries.

match: Base RPC HTTP|buyback-logs: live index failed
reason: The Base chain RPC endpoint failing; buyback indexing keeps its persisted rows.

match: token-metrics: price read failed, degrading
reason: A token price read failing; the metric degrades to null, never a fabricated price.

match: (EDGAR MNA refresh: status=degraded|\[edgar\] MNA refresh \(\w+\) DEGRADED:|late-cycle-signals: EDGAR refresh degraded)
reason: SEC EDGAR's M&A refresh did not complete in its deadline, or a month came back missing or failed validation; the producer keeps the last good data and signal and publishes nothing partial.

match: \[extract\] FRED \S+ FAILED: The operation timed out
reason: A FRED series fetch timing out; the extractor keeps the persisted real floor for that series.

match: ^\[agent:[^\]]+\] \{.*"oneShot":"timeout"
reason: An agent participant's model did not answer within its take timeout (take-runner.ts reports oneShot=timeout, nothing submitted); the member is absent from that session, never given a template take, and attendance is graded separately. An outcome of the model, not a platform failure (owner, 2026-09-25).

match: ^\[agent:[^\]]+\] \{.*"submission":"refused".*"reason":"weights_
reason: The server refused an agent's take because its model wrote a weight vector that is not the four canonical buckets (weights_required_for_bucket_weights_subject, weights_not_canonical_four); by design the member is absent, never defaulted, and attendance is graded separately. An outcome of the model, not a platform failure (owner, 2026-09-25). Any other refusal (a closed window, a roster mismatch) stays unclassified and fails.

match: ^\[judge:[^\]]+\] \{.*"kind":"refused".*"reason":"model_timeout"
reason: The judge participant's model did not answer within its timeout and the judge submitted nothing (judge-client.ts, D-A7 model_timeout). This is the model's outcome; if no attempt lands a consensus by the deadline the session publishes no_consensus, and the sessions check fails that as an unjudged publish. Every other judge refusal (credit_exhausted, credential_rejected, model_not_supported, model_unconfigured, runner) is a dead judge and stays unclassified.

match: cannot execute (UPDATE|INSERT|DELETE|SELECT FOR UPDATE) in a read-only transaction|a DELETE was refused, but NOT by the guard .* read-only transaction
reason: The managed cluster switches to read-only as its disk fills with analytics-ledger rows (8.2 GB on 2026-09-25).

match: No space left on device|could not (extend|write to) file
reason: The managed cluster's disk is full (analytics-ledger growth).

match: CONNECTION_CLOSED|CONNECT_TIMEOUT|terminating connection due to administrator command|database unavailable|connect ECONNREFUSED [0-9.]+:25060
reason: Connections dropped while the managed cluster protected itself from a full disk; also the managed cluster refusing connections (port 25060) while it restarts, e.g. the storage upsize on 2026-09-25 17:43.

match: REFUSING the boot: the append-only guard is NOT armed
reason: The guard misread a read-only session as a disarmed guard and refused boots; fixed in v0.5.1 (25006 is inconclusive).

match: POST /api/analytics/(source-acquisitions|telemetry|vintages) failed: HTTP <n>
reason: The api's analytics writes fail while the cluster is read-only or full; the api's own PostgresError is classified separately.

match: upstream prematurely closed connection|connect\(\) failed \(<n>: Connection refused\) while connecting to upstream
reason: nginx losing the api during database stalls and refused boots; follows from the database state.

match: ops\.repair_gaps\) failed
reason: The gap-repair job fails on dropped database connections.

match: permission denied for table (wallet_backfill_state|chain_day_blocks|chain_address_floors)
reason: rm_worker lacked the wallet-backfill grants; migration 0061 grants them in v0.5.1.

match: \\u<n> cannot be converted to text|unsupported Unicode escape sequence
reason: Parity evidence carried a NUL into jsonb; fixed in v0.5.1 (61ee2a0d).

match: \[analytics-producer\] (indicator catch-up|catch-up|regime failed): .*The socket connection was closed unexpectedly
reason: The analytics producer's first call to the api after a long idle gap fails on a closed kept-alive socket (production 2026-09-25 21:30 and 21:31, 29 min after its previous call; the api logged nothing and did not restart). The producer skips that pass and retries on its next schedule. Pre-existing in v0.5.0.
tolerateAfterRelease: Pre-existing in v0.5.0 and untouched by v0.5.1; tolerated at the cutover (triage 2026-09-25 21:35), to be fixed in a later release.

match: \[analytics-producer\] research failed: (The operation timed out|The socket connection was closed unexpectedly)
reason: The producer's research run could not write through the api while analytics-ledger writes saturated its database pool (production 2026-09-27/28). No partial results are published.

match: \[analytics-producer\] catch-up for <n>-<n>-<n> failed \(will retry next pass\): (The operation timed out|The socket connection was closed unexpectedly)
reason: The producer's gap catch-up could not write through the api while analytics-ledger writes saturated its database pool (production baseline 2026-09-29, x7); it retries on the next pass. Same cause as known-producer-research-failed-under-load.

match: \[analytics-producer\] fatal: (The operation timed out|The socket connection was closed unexpectedly)
reason: The analytics producer gave up while the api was saturated by analytics-ledger writes (issue 1035); it restarts under its supervisor and resumes.

match: PostgresError: canceling statement due to statement timeout
reason: The api pool's statement timeout (v0.5.1) cancelling a query that ran too long on the bloated analytics ledger, e.g. the parity sweep's full-table scan. The guard is working; the slow query is issue 1035.

match: source_value_versions_one_successor_idx|POST /api/analytics/source-acquisitions failed: HTTP 500
reason: Two regime runs overlapped after a timed-out run's writes kept executing; the ledger's unique successor index refused the second version, so the version chain never forks. A symptom of issue 1035's load.

match: telemetry submission failed \(non-fatal, canonical analytics unaffected\): The operation timed out
reason: The producer's non-fatal telemetry write timed out against the saturated api; canonical analytics are unaffected by design.

match: \[Bun\.serve\]: request timed out after <n> seconds
reason: The api's ~10 s idle timeout closing a request while analytics-ledger writes saturate its database pool (production 2026-09-25/26, during regime runs). The line names no route, so it is attributed to the load, not to the parity sweep.

match: parity_sweep\) failed.*socket connection was closed
reason: The parity sweep outlived the api's ~10 s idle timeout; v0.5.1 lifts it to 240 s for that request. (Log-line form, attributed by the job name; the api's own '[Bun.serve] request timed out' line names no route and is classified separately.)

match: socket connection was closed unexpectedly
reason: The same sweep timeout, as the dead job's own last_error (prod:gate grades dead jobs by their stored error).

match: \[projects\.refresh_wallets\] wallet \S+ live read failed, keeping last-persisted balance \(degraded\): invalid address: 0xwallet0+(aaa|bbb|ccc|ddd)$
reason: Production v0.5.4 ran RM_ENV=smoke without PROJECTS_SOURCE=live, so the projects worker persisted the hermetic fixture dataset (backend/src/projects/fixtures/dataset.ts): 4 projects, 4 tracked_wallets and 2 agent_vaults since 2026-08-07. On 0.6 (PROJECTS_SOURCE=live) the live refresh rejects each fixture placeholder address and keeps the last-persisted row. Seen on the production-shaped stage run after the v0.6.0 cutover (worker-analytics), once per fixture wallet (…aaa, …bbb, …ccc, …ddd).

The fixture rows stay in production, so this line recurs on every cron until the purge part of issue 1208 ships; every gate reports it as a warning. The match is only the fixture's placeholder addresses (0xwallet0…/0xvault0…, never 40 hex digits); the same failure on a real address stays unclassified and fails.

reason: Production v0.5.4 ran RM_ENV=smoke without PROJECTS_SOURCE=live, so the projects worker persisted the hermetic fixture dataset (backend/src/projects/fixtures/dataset.ts): 4 projects, 4 tracked_wallets and 2 agent_vaults since 2026-08-07. reason: Production v0.5.4 ran RM_ENV=smoke without PROJECTS_SOURCE=live, so the projects worker persisted the hermetic fixture dataset (backend/src/projects/fixtures/dataset.ts): 4 projects, 4 tracked_wallets and 2 agent_vaults since 2026-08-07.
